title: Prevalence of Plasmodium Parasitaemia in Blood Donors and Malaria Knowledge Survey
author: Kwame Agyemang Adusei
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pxmdpk6

steps.title: Prepare Thick Blood Smears
steps.instruction: Prepare thick blood films on clean grease-free slides.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of well mixed blood (6ul) on a clean grease-free slide using a pipette.
Use an applicator to spread the blood in a circular motion to a moderate thickness, covering an area of approximately 1cm diameter.
Label slides with the subject's code number and allow to air-dry.

steps.title: Stain Thick Blood Smears
steps.instruction: Stain the thick smears using Giemsa stain.

substeps.instruction: Stain smears with freshly prepared 10% Giemsa stain for 15 minutes.
Wash with clean distilled water.
Place slides in a vertical position on a drying rack and allow to air dry.

steps.title: Prepare Thin Blood Smears
steps.instruction: Prepare thin blood films using the spreader slide technique.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of well mixed blood (2ul) approximately 1cm from the frosted end of a slide using a pipette.
Place the smooth clean edge of a second slide (spreader) in front of the blood drop.
Hold the spreader slide at a 30° angle and draw it back against the blood drop.
Push the spreader forward with a light, smooth, and quick steady motion as the blood spreads to the ends of the spreader.
Label the frosted edge with the subject's code number.

steps.title: Fix and Stain Thin Smears
steps.instruction: Fix and stain the thin smears.

substeps.instruction: Dip the blood smear in a Coplin jar containing absolute methanol for 10 seconds and air dry.
Stain with freshly prepared Giemsa stain solution for 30 minutes.
Wash with distilled water.
Place slides on a drying rack and allow to air dry.

steps.title: Microscopic Examination and Parasite Counting
steps.instruction: Examine films under microscopy and calculate parasite density.

substeps.instruction: Examine thick films using an oil immersion and X100 objective lens.

Examine thin films first using X40 objective lens with oil immersion at the feathery tip to check staining, morphology, and cell distribution, then switch to X100 objective lens to examine malaria parasites.
Count all parasite species and forms (sexual and asexual) in relation to white blood cells (WBCs), counting 200 WBCs across 100 fields.
Calculate parasite density using the formula: NUMBER OF PARASITES/µL = (NUMBER OF PARASITES COUNTED / NUMBER OF WHITE BLOOD CELLS COUNTED) × 8000 (assuming an average of 8000/µl WBCs).

steps.title: Perform Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT)
steps.instruction: Conduct RDT on blood samples from donors and non-donors.

substeps.instruction: Take 5ul of whole blood from the labeled EDTA tube using the provided pipette.
Pipette the blood into the round sample well of the RDT.
Place four drops of assay diluent vertically into the square assay diluent well.
Read results after 30 minutes: record as positive if both test and control bands appear, or negative if only the control band appears.

steps.title: Determine Blood Groups via Tile Method
steps.instruction: Use the forward grouping tile method to determine blood groups.

substeps.instruction: Place 5ul of blood sample into the appropriate square of the tile.
Add a drop of known antisera to the sample.
Mix using an applicator and rock the tile forward and backward for 3 minutes.
Read results macroscopically based on agglutination; use microscopic reading if results are unclear.
